clue.text: A trite rule about what you could read

indicators.note: about signals the letters of a trite rule are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that books are full of hackneyed rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is written work in general, the body of material available for reading.

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught leaves, dropping out of the longer word

parts.note: a form is a school class
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl is spotted skipping her class.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a young woman or girl.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carry people or goods from place to place
second meaning: to delight or enrapture, the verb stressed on its second syllable

explanation.walkthrough: Read as nouns, a ferry and an entrance suggest a harbour; both are verbs here, and entrance means to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both conveying something across a distance and sweeping someone away with strong emotion.

clue.text: Drive away in Beetle, perhaps heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the hidden letters are read upwards, so backwards
in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone is told to chase an insect away, perhaps up towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle looks like the insect or the car to be driven away; it only houses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to force back or ward off, so it means to make something go away.

clue.text: Cared for elder, maybe, keeping at rear of ward

indicators.note: keeping means the word for elder holds the next piece within it

parts.note: an elder is a kind of tree, hence maybe
taken as written

indicators.note: rear of means only the last letter of ward is used

parts.note: its final letter is the one used

explanation.surface: A nurse looked after an elderly patient kept at the back of a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Elder reads as an older person on a ward, but it is the elder tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To have treated a patient is to have given them medical care.

indicators.note: the fish is swimming about, so its letters with those of one move around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fat rudd, a freshwater fish, is spotted swimming along.
explanation.walkthrough: A rudd is a small European freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded figure is full and curved, so it is a synonym of plump.

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than read, so it sounds like another

parts.note: tatty is British for worn and shabby

explanation.surface: Gossip that a French film star looks scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was a French actor and director, creator of Monsieur Hulot; the apostrophe s stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a celebrated French film comedian and actor of the mid twentieth century.

indicators.note: collecting means the outer letters gather the next piece inside them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of plant

parts.note: its last letter supplies the end of the answer
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a planted spy is in the end gathering intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a spy: a plant is a secret agent placed inside an organisation, and gathering information is the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy or secret operative is an agent, and a plant is one placed to gather intelligence.

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the following letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten slimmers are hooked on nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts looks like the dieters' snack but signals the letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gripped by a thing is absorbed and engaged by it, which is being interested.

clue.text: Supposed dad turned up with mum?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word for dad is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a mum is an example of a parent, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A man presumed to be the father arrived along with the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent can mean seeming rather than real, as in an apparent accident, so it matches supposed.

parts.note: the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A second musician's instrument is playing off-key.
explanation.definitionFit: A note that is sharp is pitched slightly too high, so it is off key.

clue.text: Sally interrupts me returning hospital department supplies

indicators.note: the witticism breaks into the middle of the other piece
returning means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a sally is a witty remark
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally cuts in on someone going back to a hospital ward for provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name; it is a witty retort.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is the gear or apparatus provided for a task, which are supplies.

indicators.note: accepting means the word for criticised takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lone person, panned by critics, nonetheless accepts an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the film award; it is the radio code word for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated stands alone, separate from others, as a single individual thing does.

indicators.note: left means the letter for Democrats has gone away from the word

parts.note: dafter is more daft, sillier
D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Political sniping that the sillier Democrats got left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Left reads as a past tense describing the Democrats being abandoned; here it means departed.
explanation.definitionFit: After and behind both mean following later in place or time.

indicators.note: redrafting rewrites, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the fodder, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge plan for meetings has been rewritten to bring gains.
explanation.definitionFit: Advantages are favourable circumstances or gains, which are benefits.

clue.text: Dismissed doctor jumped on one leg out of hospital

indicators.note: out of means the hospital letter is taken away from the word for jumping

parts.note: to hop is to jump on one foot

explanation.surface: A sacked doctor hopped out of the hospital on one leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dropped from a team or job has been let go, which is being dismissed.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Jewish spring feast commemorating the Exodus

explanation.walkthrough: As a phrase pass over means to skip; as one word it is the Jewish festival.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to disregard, and the single word names the Jewish feast of Pesach.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: frocks, garments that are worn
second meaning: a dressing is applied to a wound, so to dress is to bandage

explanation.walkthrough: Bandages are worn too, which keeps the surface together; dresses is also a verb meaning bandages a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names frocks and also is the verb for applying a covering to a wound.

parts.note: the state is the government of a country

indicators.note: abandoning means the word for intended gives up the letter for American

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: The administration's planned announcement leaves out the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal announcement, which is a declaration.

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for time
to renovate is to make over, so the letters of stairs are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorators finally redo the staircase, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: The painters look like decorators doing up a staircase, but they are artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters are one kind of artist, people who make pictures.

clue.text: Wonderful shade of green on vessel? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the green piece above the vessel
on the contrary reverses that order, so the vessel sits on top of the green

parts.note: a sub is a submarine
lime is a yellowish green

explanation.surface: A green paint scheme on a ship might be marvellous, or perhaps the other way about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means of supreme excellence or beauty, which is wonderful.

clue.text: Too much found in US composer's house

indicators.note: found in means the excessive piece sits inside the composer's name

parts.note: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Something excessive is discovered in an American composer's home.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cage was the American composer of 4'33".
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small country house, an example of a dwelling.

clue.text: Cleaner, for example, lifting diamonds gets prosecuted

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the abbreviation, so it reads upwards

parts.note: D is the card suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cleaner, say, caught stealing diamonds ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifting looks like shoplifting the diamonds; a char or charwoman is a British cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: To be charged is to be formally accused of a crime, which is being prosecuted.

clue.text: Boycott bowled two overs after cheers

indicators.note: after means the cricket pieces come behind the word for cheers

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, doubled

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: Geoffrey Boycott was bowled after two overs, to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England batsman, so the name reads as cricket; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a ban or prohibition, which is what a boycott imposes.

clue.text: Mess up the two sandwiches completely, initially

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for the two encloses the next letter

parts.note: both means the two

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of completely

parts.note: its opening letter is the one used

explanation.surface: Someone completely ruins a pair of sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwiches reads as food, but it is a verb meaning holds between.
explanation.definitionFit: To botch a job is to bungle it, to make a mess of it.

clue.text: Piece of jewellery made from steel, client oddly removed

parts.note: to steel oneself is to brace oneself

indicators.note: oddly removed means letters one, three and five go, keeping the even ones

parts.note: keeping the second, fourth and sixth letters of client

explanation.surface: A bangle is fashioned from steel after a strange customer is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel looks like the metal of the jewellery but is a verb, as in steel yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn on the wrist, an item of jewellery.

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the phrase next race

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of next and the start of race

explanation.surface: A runner is entered in the following race.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run scored without the batsman hitting it, such as a wide or bye.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra in cricket is a run credited to the batting side rather than a batsman.

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: Gordon Bennett and rats are both British exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: A famous figure called Gordon Bennett is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Bennett looks like a person's name, but it is a mild British exclamation of surprise or irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, so celebrity is a synonym.

clue.text: Good answer by the group showing understanding

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is a group of people, such as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A good answer from the team shows they get it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering can mean inferring or concluding, as in I gather you agree, which is understanding.

parts.note: taken as written
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: Someone is pinching the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the crime of taking another's property, which is stealing.

clue.text: Hotel east of really old part of London

indicators.note: in an across answer east means to the right, so the hotel letter follows the word for really

parts.note: so means very or really
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel lies in the east of a very old district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a lively district of central London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in the West End of London, known for nightlife and theatres.

clue.text: Top dog in Rugby, say, has red meat prepared

indicators.note: meat is prepared in a kitchen, so these letters are made up anew

parts.note: the fodder, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby boss has a plate of red meat prepared for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby here is the English public school, not the sport; say marks it as one example of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: The head teacher is the top person at a school such as Rugby School.
